failures.criterion: Plan D2 step 2 / controller skill: against a daemon with no GitHub App, `legion controller start` creates an empty 0700 gh directory, says `[legion] the daemon has no GitHub App to act as; the controller's gh acts as nobody`, and gh acts as nobody
failures.evidence: The state directory outlives a run. Scenario F (rig run-f.sh, output in the tester's PR comment): a start against a stand-in with an App wrote hosts.yml (ghs_stale_from_earlier_run); a second start on the same state_dir against a stand-in with no App printed the no-App line, yet <state_dir>/gh still held config.yml and hosts.yml and the stub Oh My Pi's `gh auth token` answered ghs_stale_from_earlier_run — gh acts as the stale token, not as nobody. controllerStartGitHubCredential (cmd/legion/controller_credential.go:107-114) only MkdirAlls the directory in that branch. Red test: TestControllerStartWithNoGitHubAppRemovesAStaleHostsFile in packages/daemon/cmd/legion/controller_test.go, commit 06f586b74ecb; `cd packages/daemon && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 ./cmd/legion/ -run TestControllerStartWithNoGitHubAppRemovesAStaleHostsFile` fails: `hosts.yml = "github.com:\n    oauth_token: ghs_stale_from_an_earlier_run…", <nil>; want none`. Low blast radius (a no-App daemon is a tmux/dev setup; the stale token expires within the hour) but the command's own statement is false while it stands.

notes: Risk, not a failure: the refresh loop's fetch (operator.do → http.DefaultClient with the loop's cancel-only context) has no per-request deadline, so a stalled connection through a port-forward blocks the tick until TCP gives up; the daemon's own appauth client has no deadline either, so this is the codebase's existing pattern, not a regression.
Doc nit: startControllerGitHubRefresh's comment says the loop logs one line per stop, but a stop on Oh My Pi's exit logs nothing (only the superseded stop does).

Observed shared-pod fact for later rounds: the implementer's embedded Postgres on 127.0.0.1:54329 is reachable from the tester's container (one pod, one network namespace); the tester started its own on 54330 rather than depend on it.
